definitions.explanation: Water vapor or wetness in the air or in materials.

examples.japanese: {梅雨|つゆ}の{時期|じき}は{湿気|しっけ}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There is a lot of humidity during the rainy season.

examples.japanese: {湿気|しっけ}で{髪|かみ}の{毛|け}がまとまらない。
examples.english: My hair won't stay in place because of the humidity.

examples.japanese: この{部屋|へや}は{湿気|しっけ}がこもりやすいので、{除湿機|じょしつき}を{使|つか}っている。{特|とく}に{夏場|なつば}は{毎日|まいにち}{運転|うんてん}している。
examples.english: This room tends to trap moisture, so I use a dehumidifier. I especially run it every day in summer.

notes:
{湿気|しっけ} refers to moisture or dampness in the air or materials.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {湿気|しっけ}が{多|おお}い (high humidity)
- {湿気|しっけ}がこもる (moisture builds up)
- {湿気|しっけ}を{取|と}る (to remove moisture)
- {湿気|しっけ}を{防|ふせ}ぐ (to prevent moisture)

RELATED TERMS:
- {湿度|しつど} (humidity - as a measurement)
- {除湿|じょしつ} (dehumidification)
- {乾燥|かんそう} (dryness - opposite condition)

USAGE NOTE:
{湿気|しっけ} focuses on the tangible feeling of dampness, while {湿度|しつど} is used for numerical humidity measurements.
